status: DRAFT - edit, commit, then lock with scripts/lock_protocol.py BEFORE running any confirmatory seed
principles: Theorem 1 and all v1.1 results (seeds 1-4 exploration, 8-11 confirmation, C2b/C4b failures, C5 specification error) are kept unchanged; nothing is re-labelled.
Every new experiment states its question, independent comparator, outcome, and acceptance or reporting rule here before it runs.
Negative and null results are reported in full; no configuration is changed after seeing confirmatory data. Any post-lock change is reported as a deviation (lipid/lock.py records it).
Classification: JNT-01 and REP-01 are verification; STAT-01 is confirmatory; JNT-02/JNT-03, MET-02, SCL-02, CERT-02 are descriptive/exploratory unless stated otherwise.

JNT-01.question: Do the closed-form pairwise bounds equal the sharp extrema of phi_i - phi_j over F_L(A)?
comparators: finite-hybrid LP with ALL vertex-pair constraints (does not use the shortest-path reduction)
solver-free extremal labeling + McShane extension + full Shapley evaluation
edge_cases: x_j = r_j on some coordinates (null players)
JNT-01.acceptance: zero comparisons above every tolerance; any failure is reported with its instance and investigated, never dropped

JNT-02.question: How many more signed pairwise orderings are certified by sharp pairwise bounds than by comparing marginal intervals?
JNT-02.design: Section-6 instances regenerated with the archived RNG streams (lipid/instances.py); matched pairs (same seed, chain, x, r, feature pair, n, L).
metrics: fraction of unordered active pairs with a strict signed certificate (pairwise vs marginal)
fraction of instances with >= 1 additional certificate
secondary: by d, n, generator, anchor law, mode, level
containment of the true difference at valid L (must be 1)
dominance pairwise >= marginal (must hold in every row)
JNT-02.reporting: mean and full distribution of the per-instance gain, including zero-gain cells; a small gain is reported as such and the corollary is then presented as a mathematical result, not as an empirical contribution

JNT-03.question: Do joint constraints (sharp bounds on phi_i + phi_j) add absolute-ranking certificates beyond Proposition 2?

subset.note: subset fixed by index, before results

comparators: exact certificate from sharp Delta (closed form) and Sigma (edge LP)
hypercube_lp.abs_margin (existing 4-LP method) on a sub-subset as cross-check
JNT-03.reporting: supplementary table; main text only if the gain is material

STAT-01.seed_note: new independent seeds; historical seeds 1-4 (exploration), 5-7 (earlier follow-ups), 8-11 (confirmation) keep their original role and are reported descriptively
STAT-01.unit: seed (one matched aggregate per seed and estimand)

inference.sensitivity: percentile bootstrap over seeds, B = 20000, rng 20261020
inference.test: two-sided one-sample t test of mean 0
inference.multiplicity: Holm within each family; Bonferroni-simultaneous t intervals also reported

P1.pooling: generators and rho_c pooled within seed

P3.strata: generator in {fa, stable_ood} (family of 2); linear and unstable_id are structural zeros (L_cert = L*), reported but not tested

P4.pooling: d, rho_c and generators pooled within seed
P4.note: nonnegative by theorem; the interval quantifies its magnitude

STAT-01.reporting: all primary estimands are reported regardless of sign or significance; if fewer than 10 seeds complete, only descriptive min-max is reported and no interval is computed

MET-02.question: How do AIW, saturation, sign and ranking certification change with the choice of sigma, with L re-certified for each metric?
scale_choices: mad (1.4826 MAD, SD fallback when MAD = 0)
MET-02.normalization: each sigma vector rescaled to the geometric mean of the MAD vector (cosmetic: intervals are invariant to a common factor when L is rescaled accordingly)
MET-02.synthetic_design: Gaussian copula with rho_c in {0, 0.9}; coordinate marginals cycle gauss / t3 / lognormal / binary(Z > 0.5), multiplied by log-spaced scales 0.25..4; rationale: with identical unit-variance Gaussian marginals (Section 6) MAD, SD and unit scales coincide up to noise and a common factor, so the comparison would be vacuous
MET-02.real_data: diabetes audit (REAL-01 split and models), sigma in {mad+fallback, sd, unit}, n_log in {16, 150}
MET-02.sanity: sigma -> c sigma with L -> c L leaves every interval unchanged (max relative change reported)

SCL-02.question: Separated from saturation of the exact interval, how informative are valid Monte Carlo bounds at practical budgets?

designs.passive: 1024 data anchors + x (Table 6 design; reference negative result)
designs.hybrid_local: B anchors at hybrid vertices z_S (|S| uniform on 0..m, S uniform given |S|) plus tau * sigma * N(0, I) jitter, + x; a fixed, NON-adaptive geometric rule that never uses f outside the queried anchors nor any interval value; benchmark instance generator, not a proposed query strategy

pilot.rule: choose the candidate minimising |median exact rho at m = 12 - 0.5| subject to median rho in [0.2, 0.8]; ties: smaller B, then smaller tau; if none qualifies, record it and evaluate all candidates as a negative result

methods.hoeffding_paper: appendix F as published (log 4m^2/alpha, overall clipping)
methods.hoeffding_tight: exact union count over sampled strata + exhaustive enumeration of strata of size <= n_k + per-stratum clipping
methods.bernstein: Maurer-Pontil empirical Bernstein per sampled stratum and side, union bound; exhaustive small strata
methods.serfling_wor: sampling without replacement with Serfling's bound; exhaustive small strata

metrics: runtime, CUDA peak memory, coalition evaluations
simultaneous containment failures with Clopper-Pearson 95% upper bound
SCL-02.reporting: if every valid method stays near-vacuous on non-saturated instances, that is the reported result; zero failures on saturated instances are not evidence of precision

CERT-02.question: Why do geometry/range certificates miss saturation when the exact AIW is near 1?
CERT-02.chain: exact >= |slope| pairwise relaxation (= min(c+, c-) per edge) >= max(geometry-only pairwise relaxation, RANGE) >= max(T3, RANGE) = uni
CERT-02.rule: a new analytic certificate is proposed only if it is a proven lower bound AND cheaper or more interpretable than the O(|A| 2^m) exact envelope

checks: clean-environment rerun (Docker or fresh venv) of tests and a declared subset of steps
numeric comparison of regenerated tables (rtol 1e-9, atol 1e-12)
REP-01.reporting: the verification report states exactly which steps were independently re-run; partial coverage is reported as partial
